<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

NIXL can now transfer KV between P and D whose hybrid KV cache group plans differ, so NixlConnector no longer needs #58207's TP-invariant planning, except for MLA. Motivated by RFC #58638. Stacked on #58207 at `e55909cad0`, #58860, #59746, #59747 and #59330; only [the last four commits](https://github.com/lucamotz/vllm/compare/77126176e8aad50c41bd402428c30686cf264f0c~4...77126176e8aad50c41bd402428c30686cf264f0c) are new.

## Claims

- Connectors say whether their peers need matching KV cache groups: `requires_matching_kv_cache_groups()` defaults to True, so every other connector keeps #58207's planning.
- NixlConnector pull between different plans is exact: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + DFlash at P TP2 ↔ D TP4 gives bitwise-identical outputs to TP-invariant plans, with 7–28% more KV tokens on D.
- This also covers plans that differ under TP-invariant planning, which depends on each side's `--max-num-batched-tokens`, PP and async scheduling.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_handshake_pp_aggregation.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_simple_cpu_offload.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_transfer_topology_sharded.py
```

On 6× H100, pull with independent plans is bitwise equal to TP-invariant push in both directions and at 262144 tokens. Under load, it shows no TTFT, TPOT or throughput cost against TP-invariant pull beyond run-to-run spread. On 2× DGX Spark, smaller models in pull and push, including D prefix hits and an MTP drafter, are bitwise equal to matching plans too.

<details>
<summary>CPU tests and byte oracle</summary>

- `test_pull_between_different_group_plans` (new) builds P and D workers for sliding-window and GDN hybrids whose plans put 2 vs 4 layers in a group, runs the real `register_kv_caches`, `add_remote_agent` and pull read path, and replays the recorded NIXL descriptors on CPU tensors: every D head and token holds P's bytes for the same layer, head and token, and nothing else is written.
- `test_kv_transfer_group_planning_is_tp_invariant` gets one row per connector; `test_layer_handshake_rejects_unsupported_geometry` gets a row for a PP push producer whose plan differs.
- `77126176e8` on main `74c5cbcd7b`: the 10 NIXL files pass with 709 tests and `test_kv_cache_utils.py` with 187, except 3 tests that also fail on main in this environment.
- A local byte oracle, not part of this PR, replays pull and push across P/D TP pairs up to 8, different plans, block sizes and D prefix hits: 2032 cases are byte-exact and none is silently wrong; the other 238 raise.

</details>

<details>
<summary>GPU: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + DFlash, 6× H100 SXM</summary>

`07c43a220c` on main `b1f229fb75`. `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` + `z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash` (7 speculative tokens), `TRITON_ATTN`, `--enforce-eager`, greedy, 4 code prompts of 1100–12000 tokens, P TP2 on GPUs 0–1 and D TP4 on 2–5 and the reverse, `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0` and `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`. Each NixlConnector pull with independent plans is compared with a NixlPushConnector run, which keeps TP-invariant plans, on the same image: texts and logprobs are bitwise equal on all 4 prompts, DFlash accepted tokens are equal, and D reads every prompt token but the last over NIXL.

| P → D, max_model_len | groups P / D, independent vs TP-invariant | KV tokens vs TP-invariant |
|---|---|---|
| TP2 → TP4, 16384 | 10 / 8 vs 10 / 10 | D +7.3% |
| TP4 → TP2, 16384 | 8 / 10 vs 10 / 10 | P +7.3% |
| TP2 → TP4, 262144 | 17 / 5 vs 10 / 10 | P +9.1%, D +27.7% |

These runs set `--block-size 592` on the TP4 engine, as the new log line suggests. Without it, TP4 picks block 304 and outputs stay bitwise equal, but D's `add agent` handshake step takes 11–15× longer and NIXL transfers about 6× longer.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Perf A/B: independent vs TP-invariant pull under load, 6× H100 SXM</summary>

Arm B is `07c43a220c` on main `b1f229fb75` (plans 17 / 5); arm A is the same build with "Let pull peers plan KV cache groups independently" reverted (TP-invariant, 10 / 10). P TP2 → D TP4, max_model_len 262144, `--block-size 592` on TP4, the flags above. `vllm bench serve` through the P/D proxy with random 8192-token prompts, run order A B B A, each run restarting both engines; greedy outputs are bitwise equal across all four runs. B − A pools both runs per arm, with a 95% bootstrap CI in ms.

| load | metric | A | B | B − A | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 at a time, 80 requests, 64 output tokens | TTFT p50 | 573.4 ms | 564.9 ms | −1.5% | [−16.1, +0.8] |
| | TTFT p99 | 623.6 ms | 607.6 ms | −2.6% | [−42.7, +22.3] |
| | TPOT p50 | 30.38 ms | 30.41 ms | +0.1% | [−9.5, +9.1] |
| 16 at a time, 320 requests, 256 output tokens | TTFT p50 | 1016.0 ms | 1013.2 ms | −0.3% | [−43.7, +16.8] |
| | TTFT p99 | 3989 ms | 4038 ms | +1.2% | [−509, +578] |
| | TPOT p50 | 17.21 ms | 17.05 ms | −0.9% | [−3.2, +3.0] |
| | output tok/s | 523.4 | 526.3 | +0.6% | run spread 3.1% / 1.1% |

D's NIXL transfers move the same bytes in both arms; under load their mean time is 77.6 vs 78.9 ms, and post-processing takes about 0.4 ms longer per transfer in B. Eager mode, so absolute numbers are not production numbers.

</details>

<details>
<summary>GB10: smaller models, pull and push, 2× DGX Spark</summary>

Build `98132d0d55`: this branch's four commits on main `d0d6e5f3a2`. P and D on one Spark, or the TP2 side across both Sparks; `--enforce-eager`, greedy. Each case differs between P and D in plan, block size or TP and is compared with the same setup on matching plans and pages, on the same image: texts and logprobs are bitwise equal, and D reads every prompt token but the last over NIXL.

- Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN): plans of 3 vs 9 groups, pull and push at TP1 → TP1 and TP1 ↔ TP2, including D prefix hits; with its MTP layer as drafter at TP1 → TP1, accepted tokens are equal.
- Gemma-4-E2B: pull at TP1 → TP1 and TP2 → TP1, push at TP1 → TP2.
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + DFlash: pull at TP1 ↔ TP2, accepted tokens equal.
- NixlConnector with OffloadingConnector through MultiConnector plans as without a connector and matches NIXL alone on prompts that share no prefix; with shared prefixes, P's CPU offload serves them and logprobs differ slightly.
- Cross-node transfers ran over RoCE: UCX `rc_mlx5`, with the reads into GPU memory emulated in software.

</details>

## Details

- **Hook:** replaces the planner's `kv_transfer_config is not None` check. MultiConnector asks the connectors it wraps; OffloadingConnector with `CPUOffloadingSpec` and SimpleCPUOffloadConnector return False, since their KV doesn't leave the engine.
- **Group pairs:** the handshake, version 15, advertises each region member's KV cache group, KV heads and tokens per page. Where plans differ or the model-wide head mapping doesn't fit every layer, layers transfer per pair of local and remote KV cache groups, in pull and push. Matched plans that the model-wide mapping fits keep today's path.
- **Who plans independently:** NixlConnector returns `use_mla`. NixlPushConnector stays TP-invariant, since a PP push producer routes layers by name. MLA, CSA-linear and PP push producers reject peers with different plans at the handshake.
- **Log:** names the `--block-size` that makes P and D pages divide, once per remote engine.

Not covered: MLA, where a GQA draft under an MLA target stays with #58471 and #59071; DCP; GPUDirect RDMA across nodes. The NIXL compatibility doc isn't updated yet.

The four commits change +700/−51 production lines. The hook can go as a small PR on top of #58207 and the NIXL commits after it, if that is easier to review. No open NIXL PR, and none citing #58638 or #58207, transfers between different KV cache group plans.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, patch and tests. I reviewed every changed line.
